title: The cart that could not arrive

model_delta.before: One mole appears complete enough for dispatch.
model_delta.after: Amount requires a specified entity before a route can be chosen.

slow_turn: Natalie separates unknown entity from unknown mass; Jeff stops the loop; Jackson keeps the cropped label beside the larger original so the missing entity remains physical evidence.

title: A number with room beneath it

model_delta.before: Understanding the mole seems to require picturing every object.
model_delta.after: An exact count relationship can be used without an exhaustive image.

slow_turn: Natalie distinguishes a representation from an exhaustive picture; Jeff compares the model to a map; the class accepts exact relationships without visualizing every entity.

title: The scanner sees twice

model_delta.before: A correct scanner tally can be labeled molecules.
model_delta.after: The tally must match the specified level: atoms or molecules.

slow_turn: Jeff preserves the correct atom tally, Henry names its entity, and Jackson connects the mislabeling to an early-closing gate; the corrected counting acknowledgement still precedes weighing.

title: What the subscript brings along

model_delta.before: A sample needs separate material for each level of counting.
model_delta.after: One sample supports different connected descriptions without changing species.

slow_turn: Natalie keeps the same sample in view at multiple descriptive levels; Jackson follows which level a receiving action needs; no atoms are physically released.

title: Two containers, one amount

model_delta.before: Equal mole amounts should have equal masses.
model_delta.after: The molar mass is substance-specific; equal entity numbers do not fix equal mass.

slow_turn: Natalie recognizes her imagined universal scoop; Kàra notices the misleading equal-container drawing; the unequal scales remain correct.

title: Natalie's fence posts

model_delta.before: A memorized factor or calculator answer guarantees conversion.
model_delta.after: Factor applicability, orientation, units, magnitude, and identity need distinct checks.

slow_turn: Natalie discovers that units alone cannot catch a mismatched substance; Ástríðr separates applicability, direction, and magnitude checks.

title: Back across the bridge

model_delta.before: Exact Avogadro conversion makes inferred sample information exact.
model_delta.after: Measured mass and approximate molar mass retain their limitations.

slow_turn: Jackson separates exact rules from uncertain inputs; Natalie reflects on what the rooftop digits did not promise; the unnamed mass card remains unresolved.

title: The quiet canopy

model_delta.before: A drawing or standard amount also determines a physical volume.
model_delta.after: The model supplies only named quantities; unspecified volume conditions remain unknown.

slow_turn: The canopy gives the group an actual break: the notebook dries, Jackson puts down his board to eat, and Henry recalls the view; a wider reference card makes the written route usable.

title: Pause before the explanation

model_delta.before: A decimal average requires a modified individual neutron count.
model_delta.after: Collection means and physical atomic masses are not neutron-count instructions.

slow_turn: Jeff identifies two distinct false leaps; Jackson preserves both in the record; Ástríðr changes the output task from construction to description.

title: Eighty, twenty, and the missing middle

model_delta.before: Two isotope categories imply equal statistical influence.
model_delta.after: Each atom contributes; the grouped weights are atom-number fractions.

slow_turn: The empty histogram position at 10.2 u separates mean from member; Natalie, Kàra, and Ástríðr keep the distribution visible before formal naming.

title: The mean moves; the counters do not

model_delta.before: Fewer heavy members determines one unique new mean.
model_delta.after: The changed total count and composition determine the mean.

slow_turn: Kàra tests whether the repaired graph calculates a new mean or merely replays 10.2 u; changing and duplicating populations distinguishes count, total, and mean.

title: A receipt that runs backward

model_delta.before: An average completely reconstructs a sample.
model_delta.after: A two-isotope mean can recover proportions, not sample size; out-of-range results expose inconsistency.

slow_turn: An archive request to recover missing batch counts motivates reverse lookup; a valid mean recovers proportions but leaves total count unknown, so the class seeks original inventories.

title: Two averages are not two atoms

model_delta.before: Two summary cards deserve equal averaging weight.
model_delta.after: Their underlying atom counts determine a pooled mean.

slow_turn: Natalie nearly averages the means automatically; Ástríðr and Jeff open the drawers, and the recovered unequal inventories let the class rebuild the pooled mean together.

title: Equal mass is a different promise

model_delta.before: Equal mass fractions can substitute for equal atom fractions.
model_delta.after: Mass and count denominators differ and must be converted explicitly.

slow_turn: Equal mass and unequal count fractions remain visible together; the class sends a complete record and witnesses its BY MASS qualifier disappear from the returned copy.

title: The little sample at the edge

model_delta.before: A small sample must duplicate population proportions.
model_delta.after: Sample descriptions and population inference have different scope; selection matters.

slow_turn: Jackson tests a suspected dispatch error but preserves two valid means with different collection boundaries; Kàra gets direct help, and Natalie records all three samples.

title: Three quantities with similar numbers

model_delta.before: Similar numerical values permit interchangeable quantity labels.
model_delta.after: Atomic mass, dimensionless relative atomic mass, and molar mass have distinct definitions.

slow_turn: Checking the neon card against its source exposes different quantity headings; Natalie reserves the advanced mass question for optional support and returns with the same useful approximate molar mass.

title: The parcel without separate molecules

model_delta.before: All moles should count separate molecules.
model_delta.after: Specified formula units support composition accounting in an extended ionic solid.

slow_turn: The class observes the extended lattice without extracting private molecular packages; Natalie links the entity choice to the model of the substance.

title: The one-box machine

model_delta.before: Local corrected numbers solve the station permanently.
model_delta.after: The shared dispatch mechanism must preserve meaning-bearing labels and assumptions.

slow_turn: The missing paper strip joins its retained return copy, locating the shared shortening mechanism; a clearly labeled test checks identity without a surprise gotcha.

title: Half a mole, all the way across

model_delta.before: One completed calculation is a completed delivery.
model_delta.after: All requested reports and their precision boundaries must survive end-to-end transfer.

slow_turn: The concise approximate-mass panel travels beside the exact count; a downstream decimal-routing switch is caught separately, and the destination acknowledgement confirms the full route.

title: A good gate sometimes stays shut

model_delta.before: A successful system always returns a number.
model_delta.after: A responsible result can identify missing information or inconsistent assumptions.

slow_turn: The unidentified parcel remains honestly on hold; Jeff prefers an inspectable imperfect station to a falsely perfect one; Jackson preserves the first versions.

title: Six biscuits, later

model_delta.before: Confidence means picturing everything and avoiding help.
model_delta.after: Portable questions, written relations, and justified pauses support independent reasoning.

slow_turn: Notebook objects return without a round of repeated morals: Natalie names what her familiar methods needed, Kàra thanks Jeff for pausing at the switch, and Ástríðr keeps the collection behind her first prediction.
